text: The Service Value Chain is the engine inside the Service Value System — six activities every service provider performs, no matter the size or industry: Plan, Improve, Engage, Design & transition, Obtain/build, and Deliver & support. This lesson covers the first three, the activities most concerned with direction and relationships.

The easiest mistake is picturing these as stations on an assembly line, each one firing only after the last finishes. ITIL 4 is explicit that this is wrong: all six activities are active in every organization at every moment, connected by flows of inputs and outputs rather than a sequence number. Engage can hand a requirement straight to Design & transition without Plan being involved at all, if the work is small and routine.

Plan's purpose is a shared understanding of vision, current status, and improvement direction across the four dimensions of service management. Improve's purpose is continual improvement of products, services, and practices across every other activity. Engage's purpose is good relationships, transparency, and understanding of needs across every stakeholder — users, customers, suppliers, and partners.

Plan doesn't invent direction out of nowhere. It depends on Engage to surface what stakeholders actually need, and on Improve to surface where current plans and products fall short. What Plan produces — priorities, architecture, policy — becomes an input the other activities consult constantly, not a document filed away after one meeting.

Improve isn't a single project with a start and end date; it's a standing activity, active at all times inside every other activity. It has a dedicated practice behind it, Continual Improvement, covered fully in Chapter 6 — this lesson introduces the value-chain activity that practice supports.

Engage works in two directions at once: outward, capturing what customers and users need and staying in contact while they use a service; and supplier-facing, managing contract performance and escalation with partners and vendors.

Plan sets direction, Improve watches continuously, Engage keeps every relationship current — together, before anything gets designed or built. Next: Design & transition, the activity that turns a planned change into something live.
